description: What must be true of the default branch before a commit lands on it. tools/check_branch_protection.py compares this against the live GitHub settings, can apply it, and holds the required_checks list against the workflows so a job cannot be green and required by nothing.
why_zero_approvals: GitHub does not let the author of a pull request approve it. With one maintainer and enforce_admins on, requiring one approval means nothing can ever merge — the same approval deadlock this repository already hit once in its durable-workflow path. Zero approvals still requires a pull request and still requires every check below to pass, so the gates are what hold the branch. Raise this to 1 and set require_code_owner_reviews on the day a second maintainer can approve; CODEOWNERS already names who that would be per path.
what_this_blocks: a direct push to main, including from an admin
a merge while any required check is failing or missing
a force push or a branch deletion
a merge with an unresolved review conversation

pending_checks.reliability-gate: Red on main since well before this policy: the architecture quality gate reports debt 568.8 -> 607.8, dependency edges +1394 and 422 new modules against a signed baseline. The private key is on the maintainer's machine, so the baseline COULD be refreshed — which is exactly why it must not be. Requiring this check today would freeze main; refreshing it would record 39 points of drift as normal. It joins required_checks when the debt is paid, not when the baseline is resigned.
pending_checks.known-debt: Reports by design and is marked continue-on-error, so GitHub records the job as a failure whenever the debt it watches is non-zero — which is always, today: 89 functions over 400 lines and 21 modules or classes past their size baseline. Requiring it would block every merge on debt nobody can pay in one commit. It joins required_checks when method-size and module-size are both green, which is the point of paying them down.

pending_checks_rule: This map may only shrink. A job listed here still runs and still reports; it simply cannot block a merge yet. tools/check_branch_protection.py fails if a job runs on a pull request and is in neither list, so nothing can be green and required by nothing.
